meta.title: Lincoln County — the money trail
meta.note: This is Lincoln County's 2026 budget, set by Ordinance 2025-21 and filed with the state. Amounts are the ordinance's maximum appropriations; the split of each General Fund office comes from its application for appropriation. The Reappraisal Fund's $76,608 is moved into the General Fund, so those dollars appear in both.

nodes.name: Office of County Clerk
nodes.note: The ordinance appropriates $198,474.72; the application for appropriation (p. 10) requests $162,710.00, split into the categories shown.

nodes.name: Office of Collector
nodes.note: The ordinance appropriates $250,203.18; the application for appropriation (p. 17) requests $255,570.19, split into the categories shown.

nodes.name: Juvenile Judge
nodes.note: The ordinance appropriates $198,083.51; the application for appropriation (pp. 44–45) requests $199,283.51, split into the categories shown.

nodes.name: County Coroner
nodes.note: The ordinance appropriates $21,874.58; the application for appropriation (pp. 47–48) requests $21,974.58, split into the categories shown.

nodes.name: Collector's Automation
nodes.note: The ordinance also says to transfer $37,321.20 to County General to aid salary; that transfer is not in this total.

nodes.name: Recorder's Cost Fund
nodes.note: The ordinance also says to transfer $5,371.94 to County General to pay salaries; that transfer is not in this total.

nodes.name: Reappraisal Fund
nodes.note: The whole amount is a transfer, paid monthly to County General, so it is counted again in County General.

nodes.name: Recycling Grant
nodes.note: The ordinance lists this under Capital Outlay and adds "transfer funds to Recycling for payroll"; the application page (p. 92) puts the $23,000 under Personal Services.
